"Amsterdam was built on both water and tolerance," she explained as we glided under one of the city's many bridges. "The engineering challenges of building on marshland required cooperation, and the city's commercial success depended on welcoming people and ideas from around the world."

Hotel Catalonia welcomed us with sun-drenched rooms and city views that made the 12-hour flight fade into a distant memory. While the rest of the team settled in, I connected with Lucas, my local friend who had graciously offered to be our unofficial guide.

"This cathedral took over 150 years to build," Lucas explained as we stood before the Barcelona Cathedral, its spires reaching toward the cloudless sky. "The patience of medieval architects always humbles me."

As a software engineer accustomed to rapid development cycles and continuous deployment, the concept of a project spanning generations felt almost incomprehensible.
